stories.headline: Jury Unanimously Rejects Musk's $150B Lawsuit Against OpenAI After Two-Hour Deliberation

key_facts.fact: A nine-person California jury unanimously rejected Elon Musk's claims against OpenAI and Sam Altman on May 18, 2026, finding the suit fell outside the statute of limitations.
key_facts.excerpt: A California jury on Monday unanimously dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI and Sam Altman on the grounds that Musk had failed to file a claim within the statute of limitations.

key_facts.fact: Jurors deliberated about two hours after a three-week trial that included testimony from Musk, Altman, Greg Brockman and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella.
key_facts.excerpt: Jurors spent just about two hours on Monday deliberating on the case, but they had spent three weeks viewing internal correspondence and hearing testimony from Musk, Altman and other tech industry executives, such as Microsoft's chief executive Satya Nadella.

key_facts.fact: Musk had sought $150 billion in damages and Altman's removal; the verdict removes a major obstacle to OpenAI's planned IPO at an $852B valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk was seeking $150 billion in damages from OpenAI and Altman's removal from company leadership. A decision in Musk's favor could also have forced changes to OpenAI's business structure and thrown a wrench into the company's plan to go public, expected later this year.

key_facts.fact: Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers accepted the advisory jury's verdict and dismissed the claims; Musk's separate claims against Microsoft were dismissed as a matter of law.
key_facts.excerpt: Musk's other claims against Microsoft were dismissed as a matter of law given the jury's findings on the two claims against OpenAI.

key_facts.fact: Musk's lawyer William Savitt said the jury 'decided that Musk was lying during his testimony about the company's origins'; Musk said he will appeal to the Ninth Circuit.
key_facts.excerpt: an appeal with the Ninth [...] to charitable giving in America.

stories.headline: Blackstone Commits $5B to Build Google TPU Cloud Joint Venture, First 500MW by 2027

key_facts.fact: Blackstone announced on May 18, 2026 a US-based joint venture with Google to offer Google Cloud's Tensor Processing Units as a compute-as-a-service alternative outside Google Cloud.
key_facts.excerpt: Blackstone (NYSE: BX) today announced a joint venture with Google to create a new U.S.-based company that will offer efficient data center capacity, operations, networking, and Google Cloud's Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) as a compute-as-a-service offering.

key_facts.fact: Blackstone is making an initial $5 billion equity commitment with plans for the first 500 MW of capacity online in 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Blackstone is making an initial $5 billion equity commitment to bring an expected 500MW of capacity online in 2027. Google will supply TPUs, software and services to the new company.

key_facts.fact: Total investment, including leverage, could eventually reach $25 billion according to people familiar with the matter; Blackstone will hold a majority stake.
key_facts.excerpt: The total investment value could eventually reach $25 billion, including leverage, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: The venture will be led by Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a Google executive of more than two decades building Google infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Blackstone has named Benjamin Treynor Sloss, a Google executive with over two decades of experience building and operating Google's global infrastructure and operations, to lead the new company as

key_facts.fact: Google's TPU client base already includes Anthropic, Meta, and Citadel Securities; the deal underscores Google's push to loosen Nvidia's grip on AI hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: Google runs its Gemini AI model on its TPUs, with Anthropic and Citadel Securities also among its clientele of TPU users.

stories.headline: Anthropic Acquires Stainless, Reportedly Over $300M, to Pull SDK Tooling From Rival Labs

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced on May 18, 2026 it has acquired Stainless, the dev-tools startup whose software generates SDKs for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Cloudflare, Replicate and Runway.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, Anthropic is acquiring Stainless, a leader in SDKs and MCP server tooling, to extend that reach even further. Founded in 2022, Stainless has powered the generation of every official Anthropic SDK since the earliest days of our API.

key_facts.fact: Terms were not disclosed, but The Information previously reported Anthropic was in talks to buy Stainless for more than $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic didn't disclose terms of the deal. However, The Information reported last week that the company was in talks to acquire Stainless, which is backed by Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz, for more than $300 million.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic told TechCrunch it will wind down all hosted Stainless products including the SDK generator; existing customers keep rights to SDKs already generated.
key_facts.excerpt: The company told TechCrunch it will wind down all hosted Stainless products, including its SDK generator. An Anthropic spokesperson said Stainless customers will still own the SDKs they've generated to date and have full rights to modify and extend them however they wish.

key_facts.fact: Stainless was founded in 2022 by former Stripe engineer Alex Rattray and is backed by Sequoia Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced Monday it has acquired Stainless, a startup founded by former Stripe engineer Alex Rattray whose software is widely used by rival AI labs, including OpenAI and Google.

key_facts.fact: Stainless turns API specs into native SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin and other languages, plus MCP server tooling.
key_facts.excerpt: Stainless turns an API spec into SDKs across TypeScript, Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, and more. Each one is fast, reliable, and built to feel native in its language.

stories.headline: Cursor Ships Composer 2.5 Coding Model on Kimi K2.5, Pricing Holds at $0.50/$2.50 per M Tokens

key_facts.fact: Cursor released Composer 2.5 on May 18, 2026, built on the same Moonshot Kimi K2.5 open-source checkpoint as Composer 2 with continued pretraining.
key_facts.excerpt: Composer 2.5 is built on the same open-source checkpoint as Composer 2, Moonshot's Kimi K2.5.

key_facts.fact: Pricing held at $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output tokens; the faster variant at the same intelligence is $3.00/M input and $15.00/M output.
key_facts.excerpt: Composer 2.5 is priced at $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output tokens. There's also a faster variant with the same intelligence at $3.00/M input and $15.00/M output tokens, a lower cost than the fast tiers of other frontier models.

key_facts.fact: Composer 2.5 was trained on 25x more synthetic tasks than Composer 2, including exercises where Cursor deletes a feature and the model rebuilds it until tests pass.
key_facts.excerpt: It trained on 25 times more synthetic tasks than Composer 2, including exercises where Cursor deletes a feature and the model has to rebuild it until tests pass.

key_facts.fact: Cursor put about 85% of training compute into post-training and reinforcement learning rather than the base model.
key_facts.excerpt: Cursor put about 85% of the training compute budget into post-training and reinforcement learning, not just the base model.

key_facts.fact: Composer 2.5 includes double usage limits during the first week of launch and is now the default model in Cursor's picker.
key_facts.excerpt: Composer 2.5 is the new default in the model picker (Composer 2 is still available if you want it). Just open the Cursor app or kick off a cloud agent.

stories.headline: Meta Reassigns 7,000 Workers to Four New AI Units on Eve of 10% Workforce Cut

key_facts.fact: Meta told staff on May 18, 2026 that about 7,000 employees will move into four new AI organizations focused on building AI-powered products and tools.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta informed employees on Monday that about 7,000 workers would be reassigned into four newly created AI organizations focused on building AI-powered products and tools, the New York Times reported, citing an internal memo.

key_facts.fact: Head of HR Janelle Gale said the new groups will operate with 'AI-native' structures and leaner management layers; the workforce overhaul precedes ~8,000 layoffs.
key_facts.excerpt: Janelle Gale, Meta's head of human resources, reportedly said the new groups would operate with 'AI-native' structures and leaner management layers aimed at improving efficiency and productivity. [...] The workforce overhaul precedes planned layoffs affecting around 8,000 employees, or nearly 10% of Meta's workforce.

key_facts.fact: The May 20 cuts will affect about 8,000 employees with another 6,000 open requisitions cancelled, an effective 14,000-position reduction.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, will layoff around 10% of its global workforce on May 20, according to an internal memo. The job cuts are part of a restructuring aimed at embedding artificial intelligence into the company's workflows and flattening its organisational structure.

key_facts.fact: US employees affected receive 16 weeks of severance plus two extra weeks for each year served; employees are urged to work remotely on the layoff day.
key_facts.excerpt: The restructuring comes as employees are urged to work remotely on the day of the layoffs, with US employees affected receiving 16 weeks of severance pay and an additional two weeks for every year worked at Meta.

key_facts.fact: Over 1,000 employees signed a petition against mouse-tracking software being used to train Meta's AI models.
key_facts.excerpt: The restructuring has sparked protests among employees, with over 1,000 signing a petition against the installation of mouse-tracking software used to train AI models.

stories.headline: Vatican Sets May 25 Release of Pope Leo's First Encyclical on AI, With Anthropic's Olah on Stage

key_facts.fact: The Vatican announced on May 18, 2026 that Pope Leo XIV will release his first encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, on May 25 covering the protection of human dignity in the age of AI.
key_facts.excerpt: The Vatican announced Monday that Pope Leo XIV's first encyclical will be published on May 25, with the title Magnifica Humanitas. [...] the full title of the encyclical is Magnifica Humanitas: On the Protection of Human Dignity in the Age of Artificial Intelligence.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic co-founder Christopher Olah will join the pope, Curial cardinals and theologians at the May 25 presentation in the Vatican's Synod Hall.
key_facts.excerpt: The encyclical, titled Magnifica Humanitas ('Magnificent Humanity'), will center on 'the protection of the human person in the age of artificial intelligence' and will be presented May 25 by the pope as well as Curial cardinals and theologians, the Vatican announced Monday. [...] To that end, among those joining him will be Christopher Olah, a co-founder of Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Leo signed the encyclical on May 15, 135 years to the day after Leo XIII signed Rerum Novarum on workers' rights during the Industrial Revolution.
key_facts.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV signed his first encyclical on May 15, a document on the protection of the human person in the age of artificial intelligence, the Vatican announced today. His signature came on the 135th anniversary of the promulgation of Pope Leo XIII's famous encyclical 'Rerum Novarum'.

key_facts.fact: Speakers include Cardinal Victor Manuel Fernandez, Cardinal Michael Czerny, Professor Anna Rowlands of Durham, Olah, and Professor Leocadie Lushombo of Santa Clara University.
key_facts.excerpt: The speakers at the encyclical's presentation will be: Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, prefect of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith; Cardinal Michael Czerny, SJ, prefect of the Dicastery for Integral Human Development; Anna Rowlands, professor of ethics and political theology at the University of Durham in the United Kingdom; Christopher Olah, co-founder of Anthropic USA; and Léocadie Lushombo.

key_facts.fact: On May 16 the Vatican announced the creation of a cross-dicasteries AI study group covering Holy See policies on AI use.
key_facts.excerpt: Over the weekend (May 16), the Vatican announced the creation of a study group on AI working across various dicasteries to exchange information on projects related to artificial intelligence 'including policies on its use within the Holy See.'

stories.headline: Italy's Lexroom Raises $50M Series B for Civil-Law Legal AI, Eight Months After Series A

key_facts.fact: Milan-based Lexroom announced a $50 million / €42.9 million Series B led by Left Lane Capital, bringing total funding to about $73 million / €62.7 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Italian LegalTech startup, Lexroom, has raised €42.9 million ($50 million) in a Series B round, eight months after its €16.2 million Series A funding. The round brings its total capital raised to over €62.7 million ($73 million). The Series B was led by Left Lane Capital, with participation from Base10 Partners, Eurazeo, Acurio Ventures, and View Different.

key_facts.fact: Lexroom is now used by more than 8,000 law firms and corporate legal teams, with a product built on a proprietary database of over six million verified legal sources.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is selling to 8,000 law firms and corporate legal teams for a verified-source legal AI built around six million documents. The product is built around a proprietary database of over six million verified legal sources, including legislation, case law and regulatory materials, which are continuously updated and structured for retrieval.

key_facts.fact: The capital will fund expansion into Spain and Germany, positioning Lexroom against US-trained, common-law-anchored legal AI rivals.
key_facts.excerpt: The funding will fund expansion into Spain and Germany. [...] The move positions Lexroom against the US-trained, common-law-anchored legal AI category, which has been the dominant venture-capital trade through 2024 and 2025.

key_facts.fact: Lexroom was founded in 2023 by Paolo Fois, Martina Domenicali and Andrea Lonza; the company argues legal AI should be built from the data layer up, not by fine-tuning generalist LLMs.
key_facts.excerpt: The company argues that legal AI should be built from the data-layer up, rather than from fine-tuning generalist LLMs. Lexroom was founded in 2023 by Paolo Fois, Martina Domenicali, and Andrea Lonza.
